claims.evidence: Witness report identifies the item as an industrial sewing machine, brand EMEL, read from the red oval badge on the left arm in photos 0-3.
The report describes the machine head and badge but does not state the stitch type or show the stitch plate, needle bar, or presser foot.

risks.risk: Machine does not power on or stitch properly
risks.proof: Video of the machine switched on, motor running, and stitching a piece of fabric.

risks.risk: Age or year of manufacture is unknown
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the serial number or manufacture date plate/sticker.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown or older age.

risks.risk: Internal gears or motor are worn or faulty
risks.proof: Video of the motor running under load with the head operating, or close-up of the open internal gear case.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having internal wear or motor faults.

risks.risk: Missing accessories such as bobbins, needles, foot pedal, or manual
risks.proof: Photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the machine.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as machine head only, with no accessories.

risks.risk: Undisclosed service history or previous repairs
risks.proof: Service records, repair receipts, or photos showing repair marks or replaced parts.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powering on and stitching fabric.
Close-up of the serial number or manufacture date plate.
response.reason: The witness names the item as an EMEL industrial sewing machine, so a worst-case price is possible; function, age, internals, accessories, and service history are unproven and priced down until evidence is provided.
